Security: consideration of whether a specific Virtual Asset is able to withstand, adapt, respond to, and improve on its specific risks and vulnerabilities, including relevant factors/risks relating to the on-boarding or use of new Virtual Assets (including size, testing, maturity, and ability to allow the appropriate safeguarding of secure private keys);

Traceability / monitoring: whether Authorised Persons are able to demonstrate the origin and destination of the specific Virtual Asset, if the Virtual Asset enables the identification of counterparties to each transaction, and if on-chain transactions in the Virtual Asset can be adequately monitored;
Exchange connectivity: whether there are (other) exchanges that support the Virtual Asset; the jurisdictions of these exchanges and whether these exchanges are suitably regulated;

Type of Distributed Ledger (DLT): whether there are issues relating to the security and/or usability of a DLT used for the purposes of a Virtual Asset; whether the Virtual Asset leverages an existing DLT for network and other synergies; whether a new DLT has been demonstrably stress tested;
Innovation / efficiency: whether, for example, the Virtual Asset helps to solve a fundamental problem, addresses an unmet market need or creates value for network participants; and

Practical application/functionality: whether the Virtual Asset possesses real world, quantifiable, functionality.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,ee620070-0c48-454c-9530-0b3abf34c142,480fd476-0932-4064-b15a-5e2299439911,,,29),25),,,,,HV0026,b071d6d7145fe585,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: ca7b40ed628e7309,"If a Reporting Entity has missed a required disclosure or the Regulator thinks there is (or could be) a false market in a Listed Entity’s Securities, what can the Regulator tell the Reporting Entity to do, and what extra ongoing duties can it add when it believes this is in the interests of the Abu Dhabi Global Market?","In these situations, the Regulator can use its direction power to require both immediate disclosure-related action and, in the right circumstances, additional ongoing duties. If a Reporting Entity fails to meet an obligation to disclose information under the applicable framework, the Regulator may issue a written notice directing the Reporting Entity to disclose specified information and to take any other steps the Regulator considers appropriate. [#SRC:f416d7fa-af65-48d6-a16f-ed11a6daadac] The Regulator may also do this to correct or prevent a false market where it considers there is or is likely to be a false market in a Listed Entity’s Securities. [#SRC:f416d7fa-af65-48d6-a16f-ed11a6daadac] In addition, when the Regulator is satisfied that acting is in the interests of the Abu Dhabi Global Market, it may direct the Reporting Entity to disclose specified information to the market or take other steps, on terms and conditions the Regulator sets. [#TGT:5ed7d470-9d48-4676-936b-d27b5c945a94] Under that same “interests of the Abu Dhabi Global Market” basis, the Regulator may also impose extra continuing obligations on the Reporting Entity, again on terms and conditions it determines. [#TGT:5ed7d470-9d48-4676-936b-d27b5c945a94]","The Regulator may, pursuant to its power under section 84 of the FSMR, issue a written notice directing a Reporting Entity (a ""Direction Notice"") to disclose specified information and to take any other steps as the Regulator considers appropriate in the following circumstances:

column2: where a Reporting Entity fails to comply with an obligation to Disclose any information under the FSMR and these Rules;
to correct or prevent a false market if the Regulator considers that there is or is likely to be a false market in a Listed Entity's Securities;","Miscellaneous . Regulator's powers of Direction

column1: The Regulator may, if it is satisfied that it is in the interests of the Abu Dhabi Global Market to do so—

column2: direct a Reporting Entity to disclose specified information to the market or take such other steps as the Regulator considers appropriate; or
impose on a Reporting Entity any additional continuing obligations;

column1: on such terms and conditions as determined by the Regulator.",DPEL,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,f416d7fa-af65-48d6-a16f-ed11a6daadac,5ed7d470-9d48-4676-936b-d27b5c945a94,,,7.5.1.(1),Part 6.Chapter 2.84.,,,,,HV0027,ca7b40ed628e7309,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

ffac0015010636bf,"If a Reporting Entity plans to publish a financial report on a set date, can it always wait until that date to share information, or does it sometimes need to disclose sooner because continuous disclosure works together with financial reporting and other disclosure documents like prospectus offers and bidders/targets statements?","It cannot assume it can always wait. Continuous disclosure is designed to work closely with periodic/financial reporting and also alongside wider general disclosure obligations (including prospectus offer documents and bidders’ and targets’ statements), so it may require earlier disclosure than the planned release date of a financial report. [#TGT:05f69230-1c8e-4359-98fe-2f92e40b5e8f] As a general position, the Listing Authority does not usually expect a Reporting Entity to disclose information before the scheduled publication date for the relevant type of document, but only if the required conditions are satisfied (all limbs are met) or if the Listing Authority does not consider early disclosure necessary to prevent a false market. [#SRC:e8a0c0b9-00fb-491e-988e-ef77853ed914] Even when a scheduled financial disclosure is being prepared, there are situations where Inside Information is discovered during that preparation; in those cases, the Inside Information should be disclosed immediately rather than being held back until the report is released. [#SRC:e8a0c0b9-00fb-491e-988e-ef77853ed914] So the practical test is whether the conditions for waiting are met and whether any Inside Information arises that triggers immediate disclosure, despite the existence of a planned reporting timetable within the broader disclosure framework. [#TGT:05f69230-1c8e-4359-98fe-2f92e40b5e8f]","HOW DOES RULE 7.2.1 INTERACT WITH OTHER DISCLOSURE OBLIGATIONS?

The Listing Authority does not generally expect a Reporting Entity to Disclose information in a document included in paragraph 117 above ahead of the scheduled release date for that document,  provided that all of the limbs in Rule 7.2.2 are met or that the Listing Authority does not consider that a Disclosure is required under Rule 7.5.1(b) to prevent a false market.  There will be cases, however, where in the course of preparing, for example, a financial disclosure required under chapter 10 of the Rules, Inside Information may come to light that ought to immediately Disclosed under Rule 7.2.1.","HOW DOES RULE 7.2.1 INTERACT WITH OTHER DISCLOSURE OBLIGATIONS?
The continuous disclosure obligations in Rule 7.2.1 also, importantly, operate closely with the:

column2: periodic/financial disclosure obligations set out in chapter 10 of the Rules; and

the general disclosure obligations under FSMR, ADGM Commercial Laws (for Listed Entities incorporated in ADGM) and international commercial and corporate laws (for Listed Entities that are not incorporated in ADGM), including Prospectus Offer documents, bidders and targets statements, etc.",DPEL,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,e8a0c0b9-00fb-491e-988e-ef77853ed914,05f69230-1c8e-4359-98fe-2f92e40b5e8f,,,119),117),,,,,HV0028,ffac0015010636bf,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: d873949d0426272b,"When a Mining Reporting Entity is preparing forecast financial information and that forecast is derived from a Production Target, how should it determine whether it must also provide disclosures about Ore Reserves—particularly where Ore Reserve estimates are being disclosed for the first time or have materially changed since the last disclosure—and what specific forecast-related items must be included in the disclosure package?","A Mining Reporting Entity preparing forecast financial information derived from a Production Target must include a defined set of forecast-related disclosures, and it should also assess whether its disclosure package triggers additional Ore Reserve disclosure obligations where Ore Reserve estimates are being disclosed for the first time or have materially changed since last disclosure. [#SRC:2c78a258-d9f2-4150-9d2c-ba681d8f9489] [#TGT:d23b7b81-8547-4159-a807-ea5be75b41b2] For the forecast financial information disclosure itself, the Mining Reporting Entity must cover the assumptions used to determine that forecast by: (i) stating all material economic assumptions employed; (ii) if it considers those material economic assumptions commercially sensitive, stating that they are commercially sensitive and explaining the methodology used to determine them; and (iii) stating all other material assumptions utilised. [#SRC:2c78a258-d9f2-4150-9d2c-ba681d8f9489] It must also disclose the Production Target from which the forecast financial information is derived, and include all information that is required to be included with that Production Target. [#SRC:2c78a258-d9f2-4150-9d2c-ba681d8f9489] Separately, if in the same disclosure context the Mining Reporting Entity is disclosing estimates of Ore Reserves (Probable Ore Reserves or Proved Ore Reserves) for the first time, or those estimates have materially changed since they were last disclosed, it must disclose the information required for such Ore Reserve disclosures. [#TGT:d23b7b81-8547-4159-a807-ea5be75b41b2]","A Mining Reporting Entity’s disclosure pursuant to Rule 11.9.1 must include:

column2: in relation to the assumptions used to determine the forecast financial information:
all material economic assumptions employed;

if the Mining Reporting Entity considers the material economic assumptions to be commercially sensitive, a statement to that effect and an explanation of the methodology used to determine the material economic assumptions; and

column1: A Mining Reporting Entity that considers certain information relating to the material economic assumptions to be commercially sensitive should refer to paragraphs 47-54 of the Guidance on Mining and paragraphs 127 and 128 of the Guidance on Continuous Disclosure.

column2: all other material assumptions utilised.

the Production Target from which the forecast financial information is derived (including all the information contained in Rule 11.8.3).","ORE RESERVES . Rule 11.6 requires a Mining Reporting Entity that is disclosing estimates of Ore Reserves (being Probable Ore Reserves or Proved Ore Reserves) for the first time, or that have materially changed from when they were last disclosed, to disclose certain information.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,2c78a258-d9f2-4150-9d2c-ba681d8f9489,d23b7b81-8547-4159-a807-ea5be75b41b2,,,11.9.2,47),,,,,HV0029,d873949d0426272b,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: f88ceff7304b0880,"When a Third Party Provider intends to change information that the Governing Contract is required to include (such as the maximum time taken for the Third Party Services to be provided or the agreed means of communication for notifications), what advance notice must be given to the Customer, and how does any written agreement between the parties affect what information is treated as contractually required in the first place?","If a Third Party Provider proposes to change either the existing terms of the Governing Contract or any of the contract information that is required to be included, the Third Party Provider must give the Customer the proposed changes no later than two months before the date the changes are intended to take effect. [#SRC:29dd8b53-d149-4830-a218-06218e05b53f] The scope of “required” contract information is determined by what the Governing Contract must contain unless the Third Party Provider and the Customer have otherwise agreed in writing; absent such a written agreement, the contract must include specified items such as the maximum time taken for the Third Party Services to be provided and the agreed means of communication for transmitting information or notifications (including any technical requirements). [#TGT:c00769cc-c353-4c08-86ed-2b5baae1cc49] Accordingly, where the parties have not agreed otherwise in writing, changes to those mandated items (e.g., maximum service time or communication means) fall within the category of changes that must be provided to the Customer at least two months in advance of entry into force. [#SRC:29dd8b53-d149-4830-a218-06218e05b53f] Where the parties have agreed otherwise in writing, that agreement affects which items are treated as contractually required content, but any proposed changes to the existing contract terms still trigger the same two-month advance provision requirement. [#SRC:29dd8b53-d149-4830-a218-06218e05b53f] [#TGT:c00769cc-c353-4c08-86ed-2b5baae1cc49]","Changes in contractual information. Subject to Rule 20.2.7, any proposed changes to:

column2: the existing terms of the Governing Contract; or
the information specified in Rule 20.2.2,

column1: must be provided by the Third Party Provider to the Customer no later than two months before the date on which they are to take effect.","Unless otherwise agreed in writing between a Third Party Provider and their Customer, the Governing Contract between the Third Party Provider and their Customers must contain the following information –

column2: about the Third Party Provider:
the name of the Third Party Provider;
the address and contact details of the Third Party Provider’s office in ADGM;
the name of the Regulator of the Third Party Provider, and details of the Third Party Provider’s Financial Service Permission;
about the Third Party Services:
a description of the main characteristics of the Third Party Services to be provided;
the information or unique identifier that must be provided by the Customer in order for a Third Party Transaction to occur;
the form and procedure for giving consent to a Third Party Transaction;
the time of receipt of a Third Party Transaction;
the maximum time taken for the Third Party Services to be provided; and
any limits for the use of the Third Party Services;
about charges and exchange rates:

details of all charges payable by the Customer to the Third Party Provider, including those connected to  information which is provided or made available and, where applicable, a breakdown of the amounts of all charges;
where relevant, details of the exchange rates to be applied or, if Reference Exchange Rates are to be used, the method of calculating the relevant date for determining such Reference Exchange Rates;
where relevant and if agreed, the application of changes in Reference Exchange Rates and information requirements relating to any such changes;
about communication:

the means of communication agreed between the parties for the transmission of information or notifications including, where relevant, any technical requirements for the Customer’s equipment and software for receipt of the information or notifications;
the manner in which and frequency with which information under this Chapter is to be provided or made available;
what information relating to the Customer will be transferred to the Customer’s Financial Institution as part of a Third Party Transaction;
the Customer’s right to receive the revised terms of the Governing Contract and any other information in accordance with Rule 20.2.5;
about safeguards and corrective measures:
how and within what period of time the Customer must notify the Third Party Provider of any unauthorised or incorrectly executed Third Party Transaction;
the secure procedure by which the Third Party Provider will contact the Customer in the event of suspected or actual fraud or security threats;
where relevant, the conditions under which the Third Party Provider proposes to reserve the right to stop or prevent a Third Party Transaction from being executed;
the Customer’s liability under Rule 20.12.6 including details of any limits on such liability;
the Third Party Provider’s liability for unauthorised Third Party Transactions under Rule 20.12.5;
the conditions for the payment of any refund to the Customer under this Chapter
about changes to and termination of the contractual arrangement:

where relevant, the proposed terms under which the Customer will be deemed to have accepted changes to the Governing Contract in accordance with Rule 20.2.6, unless they notify the Third Party Provider that they do not accept such changes before the proposed date of their entry into force;
the duration of the Governing Contract;
where relevant, the right of the Customer to terminate the Governing Contract and any agreements relating to termination in accordance with Rule 20.2.6.
about redress:
any contractual clauses on the law applicable to the Governing Contract and the competent courts; and

the availability of any alternative dispute resolution procedures, if applicable, for the Customer and the methods for having access to them.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,29dd8b53-d149-4830-a218-06218e05b53f,c00769cc-c353-4c08-86ed-2b5baae1cc49,,,20.2.5,20.2.2,,,,,HV0030,f88ceff7304b0880,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: a4585a8d826562fd,"When a Mining Reporting Entity makes a disclosure that includes Exploration Targets, Exploration Results, or estimates of Mineral Resources or Ore Reserves, what must it state about the named Competent Person(s), and what consent must be obtained before making the disclosure regarding how the information and supporting material are presented?","A Mining Reporting Entity’s disclosure that includes Exploration Targets, Exploration Results, or estimates of Mineral Resources or Ore Reserves must both (i) include specific statements about the Competent Person(s) and (ii) be supported by prior written consent from the Competent Person(s) regarding presentation. The disclosure must state that it is based on, and fairly represents, information and supporting documentation prepared by a named Competent Person(s). [#TGT:1133d38f-067b-4a0a-b325-b5c7b2512203] It must also state, for each Competent Person, whether the person is an employee of the Mining Reporting Entity or a Related Party; if the person is not, the disclosure must give the name of the Competent Person’s employer. [#TGT:1133d38f-067b-4a0a-b325-b5c7b2512203] In addition, it must state the name of the professional organisation of which each Competent Person is a member. [#TGT:1133d38f-067b-4a0a-b325-b5c7b2512203] Separately, the disclosure may only be made if the Competent Person(s) have provided prior written consent covering the form and context in which the relevant Exploration Results or estimates of Mineral Resources or Ore Reserves (as applicable), together with the supporting information, are presented in that disclosure. [#SRC:c30b96f6-edff-4774-b206-68a20fe00ba8]","Competent Persons . The disclosure made in Rule 11.12.1 must only be made with the prior written consent of the Competent Person(s) as to the form and context in which the Exploration Results or estimates of Mineral Resources or Ore Reserves, as the case may be, and the supporting information is presented in the disclosure.","Competent Persons . Subject to Rule 11.12.2, a disclosure by a Mining Reporting Entity containing Exploration Targets, Exploration Results, or estimates of Mineral Resources or Ore Reserves must state:

column2: that it is based on, and fairly represents, information and supporting documentation prepared by a named Competent Person(s);
in each case, whether the Competent Person is an employee of the Mining Reporting Entity or a Related Party and, if not, the name of the Competent Person’s employer; and

in each case, the name of the professional organisation of which each Competent Person is a member.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,c30b96f6-edff-4774-b206-68a20fe00ba8,1133d38f-067b-4a0a-b325-b5c7b2512203,,,11.12.2,11.12.1,,,,,HV0031,a4585a8d826562fd,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: 5e189c20eddb5245,"When an Authorised Person conducting Investment Business plans to use a Client’s Safe Custody Assets for its own purpose or for another Person, what specific permissions, controls, and record materials must it have in place, and what must be included in its Resolution Pack to evidence compliance?","An Authorised Person that intends to use a Client’s Safe Custody Assets for its own purpose or for another Person must operate controls that secure the Client’s position and must be able to evidence those controls through the records it keeps and includes in its Resolution Pack. [#TGT:82a79456-0923-48f0-8521-17b43774e939] In practice, this means it must (i) obtain the Client’s prior written permission before using the Safe Custody Assets, (ii) maintain adequate records to protect Safe Custody Assets when they are used as collateral or for stock lending, (iii) ensure equivalent assets are returned to the Client Account, and (iv) ensure the Client is not disadvantaged by the use. [#TGT:82a79456-0923-48f0-8521-17b43774e939] To support resolution readiness, the Resolution Pack must include records demonstrating that adequate records are kept and that the Client provided written permission for the use of Client Investments (which aligns with the need for prior written permission and recordkeeping when using Safe Custody Assets). [#SRC:803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5] The Resolution Pack must also include master lists of all Client Accounts in relation to Client investments, which supports demonstrating where equivalent assets should be returned (i.e., to the relevant Client Account). [#SRC:803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5]","The following records must be included in the Resolution Pack of an Authorised Person conducting Investment Business:

column2: Rules ‎2.7.1 and ‎3.7.1(d) (records of Client classification and Client agreements);
Rules 14.6.2 and ‎15.4.3 (master lists of all Client Accounts in relation to Client Money and Client investments);
Rule ‎15.4.4 and Rule ‎15.4.5 (adequate records and Client's written permission re use of Client Investments);
Rules 14.7.1 and 14.7.4 (assessment of appropriateness of Third-Party Agent and acknowledgement by Third-Party agent in respect of Client Money); and
Rule ‎15.5.1 and 15.6.1 (assessment of appropriateness of Third Party Agent and acknowledgement by Third-Party Agent in respect of Client Investments); and

Rule 14.11.1 and ‎15.9.1 (most recent reconciliations of Client Money and Client Investments).","An Authorised Person which intends to use a Client's Safe Custody Assets for its own purpose or that of another Person, must have systems and controls in place to ensure that:
it obtains that Client's prior written permission;
adequate records are maintained to protect Safe Custody Assets which are applied as collateral or used for stock lending activities;
the equivalent assets are returned to the Client Account of the Client; and

the Client is not disadvantaged by the use of his Safe Custody Assets.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5,82a79456-0923-48f0-8521-17b43774e939,,,16.4.1,15.4.5,,,,,HV0032,5e189c20eddb5245,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: e73ddfe65d568d47,"When an Authorised Person is calculating RWA for a credit risk exposure and has taken eligible financial Collateral for that exposure while using the FCSA, how must it reflect the collateral in the exposure amount and the applicable risk weights so that the resulting RWA amounts can be aggregated across all credit risk exposures?","In calculating RWA for a CR Exposure, an Authorised Person must determine an Exposure value (E) for each on- and off-balance sheet asset while recognising the effects of any applicable CRM, then apply the RWA formula and aggregate the resulting RWA amounts across all CR Exposures. [#TGT:5c99a9f9-b97d-4f45-834a-0562c13cf368] Where the CRM is eligible financial Collateral taken for a CR Exposure and the Authorised Person is using the FCSA, the collateral effect is recognised by splitting the CR Exposure into two components based on the latest fair value of the eligible financial Collateral. [#SRC:b8497e84-dc88-476d-8393-4486a082c9bb] Specifically, the collateralised portion must have E set equal to the latest fair value of the eligible financial Collateral, and the uncollateralised portion must have E set equal to the original E of the CR Exposure minus that latest fair value. [#SRC:b8497e84-dc88-476d-8393-4486a082c9bb] The applicable risk weight (CRW) used in the RWA calculation must then differ by portion: apply the CRW applicable to the eligible financial Collateral to the collateralised portion as if the Authorised Person had a direct exposure to the collateral, and apply the CRW applicable to the obligor to the uncollateralised portion. [#SRC:b8497e84-dc88-476d-8393-4486a082c9bb] Each portion’s RWA is calculated using RWA(CR) = E × CRW and then included in the sum of RWA amounts across all CR Exposures. [#TGT:5c99a9f9-b97d-4f45-834a-0562c13cf368]","Recognition of eligible financial Collateral under FCSA. Subject to A4.3.28, an Authorised Person which has taken eligible financial Collateral for a CR Exposure and is using the FCSA may recognise the effects of CRM of the eligible financial Collateral as follows:

column2: break down the Exposure into -
a collateralised portion with E equal to the latest fair value of the eligible financial Collateral; and
an uncollateralised portion with E equal to the E of the CR Exposure less the latest fair value of the eligible financial Collateral;
for the purposes of calculating the Credit RWA amount pursuant to Rule 4.8.3, use:
for the collateralised portion, the CRW that is applicable to the eligible financial Collateral as though the Authorised Person had a direct Exposure to that Collateral; and

for the uncollateralised portion, the CRW that is applicable to the obligor.","Calculation of RWA for Credit Risk Exposures (CR Exposures). To calculate its RWA for CR Exposures, an Authorised Person must:

calculate the value of the Exposure (represented as ""E"") for every on-balance sheet and every off balance sheet asset in accordance with the Exposure measurement methodology specified in Section 4.9 and recognising the effects of any applicable CRM;
categorise that Exposure in accordance with the Rules in Section 4.10;
allocate an applicable Credit Quality Grade and risk weight for that Exposure in accordance with the Rules in Section 4.11 and 4.12;
calculate the RWA amount for that Exposure using the following formula: RWA(CR) = E x CRW
RWA(CR)"" refers to the risk weighted Exposure amount for that CR Exposure;
E"" refers to the Exposure value or amount, for that CR Exposure; and
CRW"" refers to the applicable risk weight for that CR Exposure determined in accordance with (b) and (c); and

add the RWA amounts calculated in accordance with (d) for all its CR Exposures.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,b8497e84-dc88-476d-8393-4486a082c9bb,5c99a9f9-b97d-4f45-834a-0562c13cf368,,,APP4.A4.3.27,4.8.3,,,,,HV0033,e73ddfe65d568d47,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: 6dd44380bd02e3d2,"When an Authorised Person holds CET1 Capital instruments issued by a Relevant Entity, how should it determine whether the holding is treated as a “significant investment” for CET1 deduction purposes, and how does that determination affect which category of CET1 deduction applies to those holdings?","For CET1 deduction purposes, an Authorised Person must first classify its holdings of CET1 Capital instruments issued by a Relevant Entity by determining whether the holding is a “significant investment,” because the CET1 deduction category differs depending on that classification. [#TGT:07c1a4bc-0a9d-43a2-83b5-5e59dc8356dd] A holding must be treated as a significant investment if any of these conditions is met: (i) the Authorised Person owns more than 10% of the CET1 Capital instruments issued by the Relevant Entity; (ii) the Authorised Person has Close Links with the Relevant Entity and owns its CET1 Capital instruments; or (iii) the Authorised Person owns the Relevant Entity’s CET1 Capital instruments and the Relevant Entity is not included in consolidation under the specified consolidation framework but is included in the same accounting consolidation as the Authorised Person for IFRS financial reporting. [#SRC:c9f19d0b-d036-4cfe-88ba-7e2528a70c11] If the holding is not a significant investment, the Authorised Person must deduct the applicable amount for holdings in Relevant Entities where it does not have a significant investment. [#TGT:07c1a4bc-0a9d-43a2-83b5-5e59dc8356dd] If the holding is a significant investment, the Authorised Person must instead deduct the applicable amount for holdings in Relevant Entities where it has a significant investment. [#TGT:07c1a4bc-0a9d-43a2-83b5-5e59dc8356dd]","CET1 Deductions - significant investment in a Relevant Entity. For the purposes of Rules 3.10.7(g) and (h), an investment by an Authorised Person in a Relevant Entity must be considered as a significant investment if it meets any of the following conditions:

column2: the Authorised Person owns more than 10% of the CET1 Capital instruments issued by that entity;
the Authorised Person has Close Links with that entity and owns CET1 Capital instruments issued by that entity; or

the Authorised Person owns CET1 Capital instruments issued by that entity and the entity is not included in consolidation pursuant to Chapter 8 of these Rules but is included in the same accounting consolidation as the Authorised Person for the purposes of financial reporting under the International Financial Reporting Standards.","CET1 Deductions. Subject to the following Rules in this Section, an Authorised Person must deduct the following from the calculation of its CET1 Capital:
losses for the current financial year;
goodwill and other intangible assets as defined in the International Financial Reporting Standards;
deferred tax assets that rely on future profitability;
defined benefit pension fund assets of the Authorised Person;

the applicable amount, by reference to Rule 3.10.12, of direct and indirect holdings by an Authorised Person of its own CET1 Capital instruments including instruments under which an Authorised Person is under an actual or contingent obligation to effect a purchase by virtue of an existing contractual obligation;

holdings of the CET1 Capital instruments of Relevant Entities where those entities have a reciprocal cross holding with the Authorised Person which have the effect of artificially inflating the Capital Resources of the Authorised Person;

the applicable amount, by reference to Rule 3.10.13, of direct and indirect holdings by the Authorised Person of CET1 Capital instruments of Relevant Entities where the Authorised Person does not have a significant investment in those entities;

the applicable amount, by reference to Rules 3.10.13 and 3.10.18, of direct and indirect holdings by the Authorised Person of the CET1 Capital instruments of Relevant Entities where the Authorised Person has a significant investment in those entities;
the amount of items required to be deducted from the calculation of AT1 Capital in accordance with the relevant Rules under Section 3.11, that exceeds the AT1 Capital of the Authorised Person;

the Exposure amount of the following items which qualify for a risk weight of 1000%, where the Authorised Person deducts that Exposure amount from CET1 Capital as an alternative to applying a risk weight of 1000%:
Qualifying Holdings;
securitisation positions, in accordance with relevant Rules in Chapter 4; and
free deliveries, in accordance with the Rules in Section A4.6; and

for an Authorised Person which is a Partnership, the amount by which the aggregate of the amounts withdrawn by its Partners or members exceeds the profits of that firm.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,c9f19d0b-d036-4cfe-88ba-7e2528a70c11,07c1a4bc-0a9d-43a2-83b5-5e59dc8356dd,,,3.10.13,3.10.7,,,,,HV0034,6dd44380bd02e3d2,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: bdea13e6e19e957a,"When an Authorised Person is determining whether an Exposure should receive the 150% risk weight for being associated with particularly high risks, which types of Investments must be treated as particularly high risk, including any categories that could cover Shares or Units in a Collective Investment Fund?","An Authorised Person must assign a 150% risk weight to any Exposure that is associated with particularly high risks, and this includes Exposures that take the form of Shares or Units in a Collective Investment Fund. [#TGT:6b31cf25-ad2a-492c-87c2-2a78a8158162] To determine what counts as an Exposure associated with particularly high risks, the relevant high-risk set must include Investments in venture capital funds and Investments in hedge funds or alternative investment funds (expressly including Private Equity Funds). [#SRC:634d7695-6188-4cdb-bdd8-bc789adba744] It must also include speculative immovable property financing. [#SRC:634d7695-6188-4cdb-bdd8-bc789adba744] In addition, any Investments that the Regulator declares to be high risk for this purpose must be treated as particularly high risk. [#SRC:634d7695-6188-4cdb-bdd8-bc789adba744] Accordingly, if an Exposure consists of Shares or Units in a Collective Investment Fund and that fund is, for example, a venture capital fund, a hedge fund, or another alternative investment fund such as a Private Equity Fund, the Exposure falls within the particularly high-risk category and must receive the 150% risk weight. [#TGT:6b31cf25-ad2a-492c-87c2-2a78a8158162] [#SRC:634d7695-6188-4cdb-bdd8-bc789adba744]","Exposures associated with particularly high risks. For the purposes of Rule 4.12.19, Exposures with particularly high risks must include the following Investments:

column2: Investments in venture capital funds;
Investments in hedge funds or alternative investment funds, including but not limited to Private Equity Funds;
speculative immovable property financing; and

any Investments declared by the Regulator to constitute high risk for the purpose of this Rule.","Exposures associated with particularly high risks. An Authorised Person must apply a risk weight of 150% to Exposures, including Exposures in the form of Shares or Units in a Collective Investment Fund, that are associated with particularly high risks.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,634d7695-6188-4cdb-bdd8-bc789adba744,6b31cf25-ad2a-492c-87c2-2a78a8158162,,,4.12.20,4.12.19,,,,,HV0035,bdea13e6e19e957a,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: 16c3ee4a53c1a9f6,"How should an Authorised Person determine whether it falls in Category 2 or Category 3C when its Financial Services Permission includes Providing Credit or Dealing in Investments as Principal (not as Matched Principal), and it also carries on Managing Assets with some Dealing in Investments as Agent that is wholly incidental to Managing Assets?","The categorisation turns on which Regulated Activities are authorised and, for dealing, whether the dealing is principal credit/dealing versus agent dealing that is only incidental to Managing Assets. [#SRC:9e40803b-0d63-4d4f-a8ff-0a644cc795d0] If the Financial Services Permission authorises Providing Credit or Dealing in Investments as Principal (not as Matched Principal), and the dealing activities are not limited in scope in the specified way, the Authorised Person is treated as Category 2 provided it also does not meet the criteria of Categories 1 or 5. [#TGT:6737c8c3-06cb-4da7-bbcd-9e8650ecf66f] Separately, an Authorised Person is in Category 3C where its permission authorises one or more activities such as Managing Assets (among other listed activities) and it does not meet the criteria of Categories 1, 2, 3A, 3B or 5. [#SRC:9e40803b-0d63-4d4f-a8ff-0a644cc795d0] The explicit linkage is that Dealing in Investments as Agent does not, by itself, move the firm out of Category 3C when it is carried out wholly incidentally to Managing Assets (or Managing an Investment Fund); in that case it is regarded as falling within Category 3C. [#TGT:6737c8c3-06cb-4da7-bbcd-9e8650ecf66f] Therefore, if the firm meets the Category 2 conditions, Category 3C is excluded; if it does not meet Category 2 and it is authorised for Managing Assets (with only incidental agent dealing), it can fall within Category 3C. [#SRC:9e40803b-0d63-4d4f-a8ff-0a644cc795d0] [#TGT:6737c8c3-06cb-4da7-bbcd-9e8650ecf66f]","Category 3C
An Authorised Person is in Category 3C if:

column2: its Financial Services Permission authorises it to carry on one or more of the Regulated Activities of:
Managing Assets;
Managing a Collective Investment Fund;
Providing Custody (where it does so other than for a Fund);
Managing a Profit Sharing Investment Account which is a PSIAr;
Providing Trust Services (where it is acting as trustee in respect of at least one express trust); or
Providing Money Services; and
it does not meet the criteria of Categories 1, 2, 3A, 3B or 5.

column1: A Category 3C Authorised Person may be authorised to conduct other Regulated Activities, but it is the authorisation for Managing Assets, Managing a Collective Investment Fund, Providing Custody other than for a Fund or Managing a Profit Sharing Investment Account which is a PSIAr, Providing Trust Services (where it is acting as a trustee in respect of at least one express trust) or Providing Money Services, and the absence of authorisation for the activities specified in Rules 1.3.1, 1.3.2, 1.3.3 and 1.3.4 that are determinative of its belonging to Category 3C.","An Authorised Person is in Category 2 if:

column2: its Financial Services Permission authorises it to carry on one or both of the Regulated Activities of Providing Credit or Dealing in Investments as Principal (not as Matched Principal);
its dealing activities are not limited in scope as provided in Rule 1.3.3(1)(a)(i); and
it does not meet the criteria of Categories 1 or 5.

column1: A Category 3A Authorised Person may be authorised to conduct other Regulated Activities, but it is the authorisation for Dealing in Investments as Agent and the absence of authorisation for the activities specified in Rules 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 that are determinative of its belonging to Category 3A. Provided that an Authorised Person carries out the Regulated Activity of Dealing in Investments as Agent in a manner that is wholly incidental to the activity of Managing an Investment Fund or Managing Assets, the Authorised Person shall be regarded as falling within Category 3C.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,9e40803b-0d63-4d4f-a8ff-0a644cc795d0,6737c8c3-06cb-4da7-bbcd-9e8650ecf66f,,,1.3.5,1.3.2,,,,,HV0036,16c3ee4a53c1a9f6,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

05dc10be3be6dd06,"If an MTF lists Securities from an Exempt Offer that was made on its own platform, what controls does it need to (1) keep trading limited to the right people and (2) help users get the key information, and how does that fit with the Recognised Investment Exchange’s general rules about fair trading and access to disclosed information?","The MTF needs controls that (a) enforce who can trade the Exempt Offer Securities and (b) make sure users can access the relevant information, and those controls should operate within Business Rules designed to support fair, orderly and efficient trading and information access. [#SRC:a957fb33-ff4c-44e4-a2e7-06196b2f6b66] Specifically, the MTF must have effective systems and controls to admit only Securities from Exempt Offers made on its own platform and to identify the Persons to whom the Exempt Offer was made, so it can correctly gate trading access. [#SRC:a957fb33-ff4c-44e4-a2e7-06196b2f6b66] It must also restrict trading in those Securities to no more than 200 Persons who are not Professional Clients, meaning the venue should be able to monitor and enforce that numerical limit in its trading permissions. [#SRC:a957fb33-ff4c-44e4-a2e7-06196b2f6b66] On the information side, it must allow users of its market to obtain Inside Information relevant to the Securities, including the applicable Offer documents. [#SRC:a957fb33-ff4c-44e4-a2e7-06196b2f6b66] These Exempt Offer controls should align with the Recognised Investment Exchange’s broader admission framework requiring clear and transparent Business Rules, trading that is fair, orderly and efficient, and arrangements to help users access information made public under disclosure obligations. [#TGT:a9b5571e-2d13-4cb0-b58f-9c251e6bd215]","An MTF that admits to trading Securities that are offered by way of an Exempt Offer under MKT Rule 4.3.1 (13) shall ensure that it has effective systems and controls in place to:

column2: admit only Securities of such Exempt Offers that are made on its own platform;
identify those Persons to whom the Exempt Offer was made;
restrict trading of the Securities, to no more than 200 Persons who are not Professional Clients;
comply with MIR rule 3.9.1 (Admission to trading), as applicable in relation to the relevant Securities; and
allow users of its market to obtain Inside Information, including any Offer documents pursuant to MKT Rule 4.3.5 relevant to the Securities.","Admission to trading

column1: In order to admit Financial Instruments to trading, a Recognised Investment Exchange must satisfy the following requirements, save and except for Recognised Investment Exchanges which only admit to trading Derivatives, in which case only (a), (b), (c) and (i) apply:

column2: A Recognised Investment Exchange’s Business Rules must be clear and transparent in relation to the admission of Financial Instruments to trading on any market operated by it.

The Business Rules must ensure that all Financial Instruments admitted to trading on any market operated by the Recognised Investment Exchange are capable of being traded in a fair, orderly and efficient manner.
The Business Rules must ensure that:
all Financial Instruments other than Derivatives admitted to trading on a market operated by the Recognised Investment Exchange are freely negotiable; and

all contracts for Derivatives admitted to trading on a regulated market operated by the Recognised Investment Exchange are designed so as to allow for their orderly pricing as well as for the existence of effective settlement conditions.

For the purposes of meeting the requirements in Rule 3.9.1(c)(ii), a Recognised Investment Exchange must include in its Business Rules, or its Business Rule procedures, contract design specifications relating to Derivative contracts traded on its market which, at a minimum, include:
minimum price fluctuations (price ticks);
maximum price fluctuations (daily price limits), if any;
last trading day;
settlement or delivery procedures as applicable;
trading months;
position limits, if any;
reportable levels; and
trading hours.

The Recognised Investment Exchange must maintain effective arrangements to verify that Issuers of Financial Instruments admitted to trading on a market operated by it comply with its disclosure obligations.
The Recognised Investment Exchange must maintain arrangements to assist users of a market operated by it to obtain access to information made public under its disclosure obligations.

The Recognised Investment Exchange must maintain arrangements regularly to review whether the Financial Instruments admitted to trading on a market operated by it comply with the admission requirements for those Financial Instruments.

The Business Rules must provide that where a Recognised Investment Exchange, without obtaining the consent of the Issuer, admits to trading on a market operated by it a Financial Instrument which has been admitted to trading on another market, the Recognised Investment Exchange:
must inform the Issuer of that Financial Instrument as soon as is reasonably practicable; and
may not require the Issuer of that Financial Instrument to demonstrate compliance with its disclosure obligations.

The Business Rules must provide that where a Recognised Investment Exchange, without obtaining the consent of the Issuer, admits to trading on an MTF operated by it a Financial Instrument which has been admitted to trading on a market, it may not require the Issuer of that Financial Instrument to demonstrate compliance with its disclosure obligations.

A Recognised Investment Exchange must comply with the requirements of Rule 3.11 where it admits to trading on a market operated by it a Financial Instrument, the value of which is determined by reference to an underlying benchmark or index provided by a Price Reporting Agency.",DPEL,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,a957fb33-ff4c-44e4-a2e7-06196b2f6b66,a9b5571e-2d13-4cb0-b58f-9c251e6bd215,,,8.2.2,3.9.1,,,,,HV0037,05dc10be3be6dd06,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: a7c2fff31099d8c6,"If a Listed Entity entered into an issue (or agreement to issue) Securities without prior holder approval, under what conditions can that transaction later be treated as approved, and how does that later approval affect whether the Listed Entity needs holder approval to stay within the cap on new Equity Securities calculated using the 20% Base Amount minus Relevant Issues formula?","A Listed Entity can have an unapproved issue (or agreement to issue) treated as if it had approval, but only if three conditions are met: the issue/agreement stayed within the applicable limit, the holders of the Listed Entitys Ordinary Securities later approve it, and the Securities are actually issued within three months after that approval date. [#SRC:3f609871-988e-4e0c-921f-6e1066c630f6] This matters for the cap on new Equity Securities because issuing (or agreeing to issue) more than the maximum number produced by the formula requires approval of the holders of Ordinary Securities. [#TGT:a5d5f764-a746-4801-8e14-9584a84d3933] Once the later approval is effective for the earlier transaction, that transaction is treated as having been made with approval for the relevant approval purpose. [#SRC:3f609871-988e-4e0c-921f-6e1066c630f6] In applying the formula, Equity Securities issued or agreed to be issued in the prior 12 months are excluded from “Relevant Issues” if they were made with holder approval, and the “Base Amount” can include fully paid Ordinary Securities issued in the prior 12 months with such approval (including cases taken to have been approved). [#TGT:a5d5f764-a746-4801-8e14-9584a84d3933]","Subsequent approval of an issue of Securities. An issue of, or agreement to issue, Securities made without approval under Rule 9.7.1 is treated as having been made with approval for the purposes of Rule 9.7.1 if:

column2: the issue or agreement did not exceed the limit in Rule 9.7.1;
the holders of the Listed Entity’s Ordinary Securities subsequently approve it; and

the Securities are issued within three months of the date of the approval.","Restrictions on new Issues of Equity Securities . A Listed Entity must not issue, or agree to issue, more Equity Securities than the number calculated according to the following formula, without the approval of the holders of Ordinary Securities:

column1: Maximum number of Equity Securities = (20% * Base Amount) – Relevant Issues),
Base Amount = the number of fully paid Ordinary Securities on issue as of the date 12 months before the date of issue or agreement (the “12 months Base Amount”), plus the number of:

column2: fully paid Ordinary Securities issued in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement under an exception in Rule 9.7.4 other than exceptions (8), (15) or (16);
fully paid Ordinary Securities issued in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement under an exception in Rule 9.7.4 other than exception (15), where the agreement was:
entered into before the commencement of the 12 month period; or
approved, or taken under the Rules to have been approved, under Rule 9.7.1 or Rule 9.7.5; and
any other fully paid Ordinary Securities issued in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement with approval under Rule 9.7.1 or Rule 9.7.5;

column1: The Base Amount may include fully paid Ordinary Securities issued in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement under an agreement to issue Securities within Rule 9.7.4 exception (14) where the issue is subsequently approved under Rule 9.7.1.

column2: partly paid Ordinary Securities that became fully paid in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement,

column1: but subtracting the number of fully paid Ordinary Securities cancelled in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement.
Relevant Issues = the number of Equity Securities issued, or agreed to be issued, in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement to issue other than:

column2: with the approval of the holders of its Ordinary Securities under Rule 9.7.1 or Rule 9.7.5; or

under an exception in Rule 9.7.4.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,3f609871-988e-4e0c-921f-6e1066c630f6,a5d5f764-a746-4801-8e14-9584a84d3933,,,9.7.5,9.7.1,,,,,HV0038,a7c2fff31099d8c6,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: f6f4407ec6bd7977,"When an Authorised Person evaluates its Exposure to interest rate risk arising from its Non Trading Book activities, what specific interest-rate shock scenario must be included, and how should the evaluation be handled if the Authorised Person has balance sheet positions in more than one currency?","An Authorised Person’s evaluation of its Exposure to the interest rate risk arising from its Non Trading Book activities must include a defined stress scenario and, where relevant, be performed on a currency-by-currency basis. [#TGT:9f5db2ba-19a5-4149-b8c0-f470ec9e54e3] Specifically, the evaluation must cover the impact of a sudden and unexpected parallel shift in interest rates of 200 basis points, assessed in both directions (i.e., an upward and a downward move). [#SRC:0dd318fb-6509-4aaf-96be-2ee00073b4c6] In addition, if the Authorised Person has balance sheet positions in different currencies, it must measure its risk Exposures separately in each material currency, rather than only producing a single aggregated measure across currencies. [#TGT:9f5db2ba-19a5-4149-b8c0-f470ec9e54e3] Taken together, this means the required 200-basis-point parallel-rate shock (up and down) must be applied within the evaluation framework used for Non Trading Book interest rate risk, and the resulting risk Exposures must be determined for each material currency where multi-currency balance sheet positions exist. [#SRC:0dd318fb-6509-4aaf-96be-2ee00073b4c6] [#TGT:9f5db2ba-19a5-4149-b8c0-f470ec9e54e3]",The evaluation under Rule 7.2.1 must cover the effect of a sudden and unexpected parallel change in interest rates of 200 basis points in both directions.,An Authorised Person must carry out an evaluation of its Exposure to the interest rate risk arising from its Non Trading Book activities. An Authorised Person with balance sheet positions in different currencies must measure its risk Exposures in each of the material currencies.,DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,0dd318fb-6509-4aaf-96be-2ee00073b4c6,9f5db2ba-19a5-4149-b8c0-f470ec9e54e3,,,7.2.2.(1),7.2.1,,,,,HV0039,f6f4407ec6bd7977,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

5f62d3cce6a13e8e,"For a Domestic Fund that is treated as an Exempt Fund because it is privately placed only, limited to Professional Clients, and has a minimum initial subscription of at least US$50,000 while not meeting the conditions to be a Qualified Investor Fund, what must the Fund Manager do if the fund later cannot continue to meet the conditions needed to remain an Exempt Fund, and what alternative reclassification options are available?","A Domestic Fund that qualifies as an Exempt Fund on the basis that its Units are offered only by private placement, all Unitholders meet the criteria to be classified as Professional Clients, and each person’s initial subscription is at least US$50,000 (and it is not a Qualified Investor Fund) is treated as an Exempt Fund for these purposes. [#TGT:739bcd07-b23a-4057-98eb-1f81fab280f8] If that Exempt Fund later can no longer meet the relevant conditions required for it to be classified as an Exempt Fund, the Fund Manager is required to apply for the winding up of that Fund. [#SRC:6e2b3cea-7166-4cff-a20a-f10f87ba8b03] As an alternative to winding up, the Fund Manager may instead have the Fund moved to the classification of a Public Fund, but doing so requires satisfying the requirements and formalities that apply specifically to a Public Fund. [#SRC:6e2b3cea-7166-4cff-a20a-f10f87ba8b03] Separately, an Exempt Fund may choose to convert to a Qualified Investor Fund, but only if it meets the conditions applicable to a Qualified Investor Fund (which is distinct from the Domestic Fund scenario described where it does not satisfy those conditions). [#SRC:6e2b3cea-7166-4cff-a20a-f10f87ba8b03] [#TGT:739bcd07-b23a-4057-98eb-1f81fab280f8]","If an Exempt Fund can no longer meet the relevant conditions set out in Rule ‎3.3.3 to be classified as an Exempt Fund, the Fund Manager of that Fund is required, under Section 112 of the FSMR, to apply for the winding up of that Fund. Alternatively, the Fund Manager may have that Fund moved to the classification of a Public Fund, which requires the satisfaction of the requirements and formalities specific to that type of Fund. An Exempt Fund may also, if it wishes to, convert to a Qualified Investor Fund provided it meets the conditions applicable to a Qualified Investor Fund in Rule ‎3.3.4.","A Domestic Fund is an Exempt Fund, if:

column2: its Units are offered to persons only by way of a private placement;
all its Unitholders are persons who meet the criteria to be classified as Professional Clients; and
the initial subscription to be paid by a person to become a Unitholder is at least US$50,000,

column1: and it does not satisfy the conditions in Rule ‎3.3.4 below to be a Qualified Investor Fund.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,6e2b3cea-7166-4cff-a20a-f10f87ba8b03,739bcd07-b23a-4057-98eb-1f81fab280f8,,,PART 5.14.1.Guidance.1,PART 2.3.3.3.(1),,,,,HV0040,5f62d3cce6a13e8e,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

3680a608c39c6edf,"When an Authorised Person (and its participants) intends to use a delivery and/or storage facility for Accepted Spot Commodities in a jurisdiction outside the ADGM, what conditions must that facility satisfy so it can be treated as an eligible “appropriate jurisdiction” facility, and what ongoing compliance features must be in place?","An Authorised Person, and its participants, may use delivery and/or storage facilities for Accepted Spot Commodities either within the ADGM or in another jurisdiction, but use outside the ADGM is only permissible where the facility meets the specified requirements for an “appropriate jurisdiction” facility. [#SRC:4230a066-37c4-4630-bb93-d9a0ed5bc81b] For a facility operating from outside ADGM to qualify, it must operate under rules and regulations equivalent to those applying in the Abu Dhabi Global Market. [#TGT:dda13926-2cce-4e09-a50f-508bd4257bd5] In addition, the facility must maintain ongoing compliance and controls, including: it must at all times comply with all applicable laws in the relevant jurisdiction or elsewhere (explicitly including port conditions, customs, anticorruption, and taxation requirements, plus any other applicable rules). [#TGT:dda13926-2cce-4e09-a50f-508bd4257bd5] It must adhere to appropriate international standards for storage and delivery mechanisms (including IOSCO Good and Sound Practices) and hold OHSAS 18001 Health & Safety Management or equivalent certification standards. [#TGT:dda13926-2cce-4e09-a50f-508bd4257bd5] It must also have appropriate audit and control arrangements for inventories, deliveries, and physical infrastructure, and appropriate insurance covering operational, security, fraud, natural disasters, and other applicable risks. [#TGT:dda13926-2cce-4e09-a50f-508bd4257bd5]","An Authorised Person, and its participants, must only use delivery and/or storage facilities for Accepted Spot Commodities from:

column2: within the ADGM, or

other appropriate jurisdictions that can meet the requirements of Rule 22.4.2.","For the purposes of Rule 22.4.1, any delivery and/or storage facility used by an Authorised Person must be a facility in relation to which –
where the delivery and/or storage facility operates from outside ADGM, it operates under rules and regulations equivalent to those applying in the Abu Dhabi Global Market;
the delivery and/or storage facility will, at all times, comply with all applicable laws in the relevant jurisdiction or elsewhere, including in particular and without limitation:
local port conditions;
local, national and global customs requirements;
local, national and global anticorruption laws;
local, national and global taxation requirements; and
any other applicable rules and regulations;
the delivery and/or storage facility adheres to:
appropriate international standards for storage and delivery mechanisms, including with regard to IOSCO’s Good and Sound Practices; and
OHSAS 18001 Health & Safety Management or equivalent certification standards;
it has appropriate audit and control arrangements in place, in relation to inventories, deliveries and physical infrastructure; and

it has appropriate insurance arrangements in place to cover operational, security, fraud, natural disasters and other applicable risks.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,4230a066-37c4-4630-bb93-d9a0ed5bc81b,dda13926-2cce-4e09-a50f-508bd4257bd5,,,22.4.1,22.4.2,,,,,HV0041,3680a608c39c6edf,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: a346741805e67f29,"When the Regulator receives the required notice that would ordinarily trigger it to inform Host Regulator(s) of its intent to use the passporting procedures for a Passported Fund, in what circumstances may the Regulator refrain from sending that notice, and if it does proceed, what are the timing and follow-on steps tied to Host Regulator confirmation and the Register of Passported Funds?","The Regulator’s ability to progress passporting notifications is conditional: even where it would ordinarily send a notice to Host Regulator(s) about its intent to use the passporting procedures, it must refrain from transmitting the relevant notice if it considers the Fund Manager or the Public Fund is not compliant, or may become non-compliant, with applicable legislation (including these Rules), or if refraining is necessary and appropriate to meet the Regulator’s objectives. [#SRC:02c6d009-e171-41d6-adac-aaaaf2b66e5a] If the Regulator does proceed (i.e., it does not apply the above grounds to refrain), it must, within five Business Days after receiving the triggering notice, provide notice of its intent to use the passporting procedures to the Host Regulator(s) in each relevant Host Jurisdiction where the Passported Fund is intended to be Promoted. [#TGT:3c548ffe-2bd8-478f-8ddc-d55a1eb83d6e] After the relevant Host Regulator confirms that its Register of Passported Funds has been updated to include the Passported Fund’s details, the Regulator must then promptly (i) publish the Passported Fund’s details on the Register of Passported Funds and (ii) notify the Fund Manager that registration on that Register is complete. [#TGT:3c548ffe-2bd8-478f-8ddc-d55a1eb83d6e]","The Regulator shall not transmit a notice under Rule 3.2.4‎(a):

column2: if it considers that the Fund Manager or the Public Fund does not comply with, or it has reasonable grounds for determining that the Fund Manager or the Public Fund may in the future not comply with, applicable legislation, including these Rules; or
if it considers that it is necessary and appropriate to refrain from doing so in order to meet its objectives.","The Regulator shall:

Within five Business Days of receipt of the notice set out in Rule 3.2.2, and subject to Rule 3.2.5, provide notice of the intent to use the passporting procedures under these Rules to the Host Regulator(s) in the relevant Host Jurisdiction(s) where the Passported Fund is intended to be Promoted; and
promptly following confirmation from the relevant Host Regulator that its respective Register of Passported Funds has been updated to include the details of the Passported Fund:
publish the details of the Passported Fund on the Register of Passported Funds; and

notify the Fund Manager that registration on the Register of Passported Funds is complete.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,02c6d009-e171-41d6-adac-aaaaf2b66e5a,3c548ffe-2bd8-478f-8ddc-d55a1eb83d6e,,,3.2.5,3.2.4,,,,,HV0042,a346741805e67f29,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: e2fc874bfacea533,"For an Authorised Person operating as a Branch, what ongoing prudential resource standards apply and what specific reporting and notification actions must it take toward the Regulator, given how the Rules are applied by operating model?","An Authorised Person operating as a Branch is within the scope of the Rules that apply specifically to Branches, rather than the set that applies to a Domestic Firm. [#SRC:125f72ef-4896-42ec-90ce-f01b83fa15b6] Within that Branch scope, it must maintain adequate liquidity and financial resources at all times, calibrated to the nature, size, and complexity of its business, so that there is no significant risk it cannot meet liabilities when due. [#TGT:9fbb61f7-59fe-4340-85f8-ab6b9e7fb03c] It must also comply continuously with its Home State Regulator’s prudential requirements. [#TGT:9fbb61f7-59fe-4340-85f8-ab6b9e7fb03c] In addition, it has two direct obligations to the Regulator that link its Home State prudential regime to local oversight: (1) it must provide the Regulator with a copy of every capital adequacy summary report and Leverage Ratio report that it submits to its Home State Regulator, and it must do so within ten business days after the due date for submission to the Home State Regulator; and (2) if it anticipates or experiences any breach of Home State prudential requirements, it must notify the Regulator immediately and include any relevant documents. [#TGT:9fbb61f7-59fe-4340-85f8-ab6b9e7fb03c]","In this Section the Rules apply to an Authorised Person in any Category as follows:

column2: Rule 3.2.2 applies to an Authorised Person operating as a Branch; and
Rules 3.2.3 to 3.2.5 apply to an Authorised Person operating as a Domestic Firm.","Branches – general requirements. An Authorised Person that is a Branch must:

ensure that it has and maintains, at all times, liquid assets and access to financial resources which are adequate in relation to the nature, size and complexity of its business both as to amount and quality to ensure that there is no significant risk that liabilities cannot be met as they fall due;
ensure that it complies at all times with its Home State Regulator's prudential requirements;

submit to the Regulator a copy of every capital adequacy summary report and Leverage Ratio report submitted to its Home State Regulator within ten business days of the due date for submission to that regulator; and

in the event of any anticipated or actual breach of any prudential requirements set by its Home State Regulator, notify the Regulator immediately with any relevant documents.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,125f72ef-4896-42ec-90ce-f01b83fa15b6,9fbb61f7-59fe-4340-85f8-ab6b9e7fb03c,,,3.2.1,3.2.2,,,,,HV0043,e2fc874bfacea533,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: 35357c6e2759b1b1,"If a Fund Manager of a Domestic Fund wants to do the Fund’s administration work itself, what must be kept separate, and what does the Fund Manager still have to do to make sure the Fund’s operating risks are properly dealt with (including considering Fund Administrators, Eligible Custodians, and any prime brokers)?","If a Fund Manager of a Domestic Fund performs fund administration for the Fund, it is only permitted where the risk management function and the portfolio function are adequately separated. [#SRC:5cba2a1e-1340-4401-a5c7-23c937abe4fc] Even in that situation, the Fund Manager must ensure that the risks inherent in running the Fund are adequately addressed. [#TGT:b6eb6967-279e-4da2-9b77-1f703f2597f7] In doing so, the Fund Manager must take into account the nature of its strategies and investment process, and also consider the role of Fund Administrators and Eligible Custodians and, if they are appointed, prime brokers. [#TGT:b6eb6967-279e-4da2-9b77-1f703f2597f7] This means the Fund Manager cannot treat “doing administration in-house” as a substitute for risk management; it must maintain the required separation between risk management and portfolio activities while evaluating how administration, custody, and any prime brokerage arrangements affect the Fund’s operational risks. [#SRC:5cba2a1e-1340-4401-a5c7-23c937abe4fc] [#TGT:b6eb6967-279e-4da2-9b77-1f703f2597f7]",A Fund Manager of a Domestic Fund may be able to perform fund administration for the Fund in circumstances where risk management and portfolio functions are adequately separated (Rule 12.3.10).,"Risk management. A Fund Manager of a Domestic Fund must ensure that the risks inherent in the operation of a Fund are adequately addressed, with due regard to the nature of the strategies and investment process employed by the Fund Manager and the role of Fund Administrators and Eligible Custodians and where appointed, prime brokers.",DPEL,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,5cba2a1e-1340-4401-a5c7-23c937abe4fc,b6eb6967-279e-4da2-9b77-1f703f2597f7,,,PART 5.12.3.7.Guidance.1,PART 5.12.3.10,,,,,HV0044,35357c6e2759b1b1,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

5f7240dae9e51d81,"For an Authorised Person exposed to the risk of foreign currencies and gold under an Islamic Contract, when is it permitted not to calculate a Foreign Exchange Risk Capital Requirement, and what quantitative tests must it apply using its Foreign Currency business and overall net open position relative to Capital Resources?","An Authorised Person that has exposure to the risk of foreign currencies and gold under any Islamic Contract is generally required to calculate a Foreign Exchange Risk Capital Requirement. [#SRC:6a51fe1f-d0d3-42f6-b369-4e9345775696] However, it is permitted not to perform that calculation if it satisfies both quantitative conditions tied to Capital Resources. [#TGT:79d3cd2f-93a5-4f25-af68-c67e7fd4cb97] Specifically, it must determine its “Foreign Currency business” by taking the greater of (i) the sum of its gross long positions and (ii) the sum of its gross short positions across all Foreign Currencies, and confirm that this amount does not exceed 100% of its Capital Resources. [#TGT:79d3cd2f-93a5-4f25-af68-c67e7fd4cb97] In addition, it must confirm that its overall net open position does not exceed 2% of its Capital Resources. [#TGT:79d3cd2f-93a5-4f25-af68-c67e7fd4cb97] If either threshold is breached, the exemption is unavailable and the Authorised Person must calculate the Foreign Exchange Risk Capital Requirement notwithstanding that the exposure arises under an Islamic Contract and includes foreign currencies and gold. [#SRC:6a51fe1f-d0d3-42f6-b369-4e9345775696] [#TGT:79d3cd2f-93a5-4f25-af68-c67e7fd4cb97]","Market risk. An Authorised Person which is exposed to the risk of foreign currencies and gold under any Islamic Contract, must calculate its Foreign Exchange Risk Capital Requirement in accordance with PRU Rule 5.6.2.","An Authorised Person need not calculate a Foreign Exchange Risk Capital Requirement if:

column2: its Foreign Currency business, defined as the greater of the sum of its gross long positions and the sum of its gross short positions in all Foreign Currencies, does not exceed 100% of Capital Resources as defined in Chapter 3; and

its overall net open position as defined in Rule A6.4.4 does not exceed 2% of its Capital Resources as defined in Chapter 3.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,6a51fe1f-d0d3-42f6-b369-4e9345775696,79d3cd2f-93a5-4f25-af68-c67e7fd4cb97,,,5.4.11,5.6.2,,,,,HV0045,5f7240dae9e51d81,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: 5705e32a1a365390,"When the Regulator discloses Confidential Information to a criminal law enforcement agency (in the U.A.E or elsewhere) specifically to support a criminal investigation or criminal proceedings, what conditions must be met for the disclosure to be permitted, and does that scenario remain subject to the separate requirements that otherwise apply to such disclosures?","A disclosure by the Regulator of Confidential Information to a criminal law enforcement agency (whether in the U.A.E or otherwise) for the purpose of a criminal investigation or criminal proceedings is permitted where it is made to facilitate the carrying out of a Public Function and falls within the permitted disclosure bases described for such facilitation. [#TGT:c143e65b-358c-4ac8-855c-546a1c91e4d1] In particular, the disclosure may be made to a criminal law enforcement agency for that criminal-investigation/proceedings purpose as one of the listed recipient-and-purpose categories, and it must be for the purpose of assisting that recipient’s performance of its functions and powers. [#TGT:c143e65b-358c-4ac8-855c-546a1c91e4d1] Separately, where the Regulator makes this specific type of disclosure to a criminal law enforcement agency for a criminal investigation or criminal proceedings, that disclosure is expressly carved out from being subject to the additional requirements that would otherwise apply under the separate requirements referenced for disclosures made on that basis. [#SRC:3ea3d5aa-2378-40cd-ab7a-f454859a385c] Accordingly, the Regulator should frame the disclosure as facilitating a Public Function and within the criminal law enforcement agency category, while recognizing that the usual additional requirements do not apply to this particular criminal-law-enforcement disclosure scenario. [#TGT:c143e65b-358c-4ac8-855c-546a1c91e4d1] [#SRC:3ea3d5aa-2378-40cd-ab7a-f454859a385c]","Disclosure to a criminal law enforcement agency. Importantly, disclosure of Confidential Information by the Regulator to a criminal law enforcement agency, whether in the U.A.E or otherwise, for the purpose of any criminal investigation or criminal proceedings under paragraph 199(1)(b)(v) is not subject to the requirements under section 199(2).","Subject to subsection (2), the Regulator may disclose Confidential Information for the purpose of facilitating the carrying out of a Public Function where such disclosure is—

column2: permitted or required under any enactment applicable to the Regulator, including, for the avoidance of doubt, any applicable international obligations;
made to—
the ADGM Registrar of Companies;
a Non-Abu Dhabi Global Market Regulator;

a governmental or regulatory authority exercising powers and performing functions relating to anti-money laundering, counter terrorist financing or sanctions compliance, whether in the Abu Dhabi Global Market or otherwise;
a self regulatory body or organisation exercising and performing powers and functions in relation to financial services, whether in the Abu Dhabi Global Market or otherwise;
a criminal law enforcement agency, whether in the U.A.E or otherwise, for the purpose of any criminal investigation or criminal proceedings; or
a civil law enforcement agency or body, whether in the Abu Dhabi Global Market, U.A.E or otherwise;

column1: for the purpose of assisting the performance by any such person of its functions and powers; or

column2: made in good faith for the purposes of the exercise of the functions and powers of the Regulator or in order to further the Regulator's objectives.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,3ea3d5aa-2378-40cd-ab7a-f454859a385c,c143e65b-358c-4ac8-855c-546a1c91e4d1,,,3.3.5,Part 16.199.(1),,,,,HV0046,5705e32a1a365390,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: 44f10b5136e2eacc,"When a Petroleum Reporting Entity identifies new material estimates of Prospective Resources, Contingent Resources or Petroleum Reserves that have not previously been disclosed and must disclose them immediately, what specific content must be included in that disclosure, including how the entity should address permits/licences, the new data, the effect on estimates, and any updates to previously disclosed information?","If a Petroleum Reporting Entity has new material estimates of Prospective Resources, Contingent Resources or Petroleum Reserves that have not previously been disclosed, it must disclose those estimates immediately. [#TGT:1d41da19-7d47-42e7-baf3-28af0f6c1c12] When making that disclosure, the entity must ensure the disclosure includes several specific elements so the market can understand both the basis for the new estimates and what has changed from earlier disclosures. [#SRC:a9ffc27d-5147-4066-826f-22c25cd1e704] At a minimum, the disclosure must: (i) state the types of permits or licences the Petroleum Reporting Entity holds that relate to the estimates; (ii) explain the new data and information; (iii) explain how that new data and information has affected the estimates of Prospective Resources, Contingent Resources or Petroleum Resources; and (iv) describe any changes or additions to information the entity previously disclosed about Prospective Resources, Contingent Resources, and Petroleum Reserves. [#SRC:a9ffc27d-5147-4066-826f-22c25cd1e704] This content expectation applies in the context of the immediate disclosure obligation for new material estimates that were not previously disclosed. [#TGT:1d41da19-7d47-42e7-baf3-28af0f6c1c12]","A Petroleum Reporting Entity making a disclosure under Rule 12.6.1 must ensure the disclosure contains:

column2: the types of permits or licences held by the Petroleum Reporting Entity relating to the estimates;
an explanation of the new data and information;
an explanation of how the new data and information has affected the estimates of Prospective Resources, Contingent Resources or Petroleum Resources; and
any changes or additions to the information previously disclosed relating to:
Prospective Resources under Rules 12.8.1(1) to 12.8.1(4);
Contingent Resources under Rules 12.10.1(1) to 12.10.1(5); and

Petroleum Reserves under Rules 12.12.1(1) to 12.12.1(7).","A Petroleum Reporting Entity must immediately disclose any new material estimates of Prospective Resources, Contingent Resources or Petroleum Reserves that have not previously been disclosed.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,a9ffc27d-5147-4066-826f-22c25cd1e704,1d41da19-7d47-42e7-baf3-28af0f6c1c12,,,12.6.2,12.6.1,,,,,HV0047,44f10b5136e2eacc,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

column1: 5da11b6862d3a3ee,"When an Issuer wants to use an MTF as the primary trading venue for Digital Securities offered and issued by way of an Exempt Offer (with membership and trading limited to non-retail clients only), what must the Issuer include in its Exempt Offer document so that the Regulator can treat those Digital Securities as Securities, and how may the Regulator impose conditions when doing so?","For an Issuer seeking admission of its Digital Securities to trading on an MTF through an Exempt Offer (in a setting where MTF participation is restricted to non-retail clients), the Issuer must ensure the Exempt Offer document contains all information that is required for that Exempt Offer so the FSRA can deem the Digital Securities to be Securities for the relevant regulatory purposes. [#SRC:1ad93605-b12d-4852-9c5f-18d8569c27a7] This means the compliance focus is on completeness of the Exempt Offer document as the prerequisite for the deeming outcome needed for MTF trading in this context. [#SRC:1ad93605-b12d-4852-9c5f-18d8569c27a7] Separately, the Regulator has an express power, via written notice, to deem an investment that is not otherwise a Security to be a Security for the purposes of the Regulations and the Rules made under them. [#TGT:95497208-1e94-4b51-8ff3-d9e77f64177c] When exercising that deeming power, the Regulator may attach any terms and conditions it considers appropriate, so the Issuer should be prepared for the deeming decision to be conditional rather than unconditional. [#TGT:95497208-1e94-4b51-8ff3-d9e77f64177c]","DIGITAL SECURITIES & TRADING VENUES

MTFs may operate as a primary trading venue for Digital Securities offered and issued by way of an Exempt Offer, provided that membership and trading is limited to non-retail clients only.  As set out in paragraphs 16 and 32 of this Guidance, an Issuer wishing to make an Exempt Offer in order to have its Digital Securities admitted to trading on an MTF will need to ensure that it includes all required information in its Exempt Offer document in order to allow FSRA to deem the Digital Securities as Securities pursuant to section 58(2)(b) of FSMR.","Without limiting the generality of its powers, the Regulator may, by written notice—

column2: exclude the application of any requirements; or
deem any investment which is not a Security to be a Security for the purposes of these Regulations and the Rules made under these Regulations;

column1: subject to such terms and conditions as it may consider appropriate.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,1ad93605-b12d-4852-9c5f-18d8569c27a7,95497208-1e94-4b51-8ff3-d9e77f64177c,,,46),Part 6.Chapter 1.58.(2),,,,,HV0048,5da11b6862d3a3ee,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

3e2ee2e30ce215da,"For an Authorised Person conducting Investment Business, how should the Resolution Pack reflect the periodic reconciliation and counting activities required for Client Accounts held with Third Party Agents and for Safe Custody Assets (including any involvement of a Nominee Company), and what minimum frequencies apply?","An Authorised Person conducting Investment Business should ensure its Resolution Pack includes the most recent reconciliation records that evidence it is meeting the required reconciliation and counting cadence for Third Party Agent-held Client Accounts and for Safe Custody Assets. [#SRC:803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5] In practice, this means the pack should contain the latest reconciliations of Client Money and Client Investments, aligned to the underlying operational duties to (i) reconcile records of Client Accounts held with Third Party Agents against the Third Party Agents’ monthly statements at least every calendar month, and (ii) perform six‑monthly controls over Safe Custody Assets and related ledgers.
