In other words, the firm should not treat outsourcing as transferring responsibility: it must be able to show both that the outsourced assessments align with the PRA’s expanded expectations and that the outsourcer’s methods are controlled, validated, and overseen through effective firm-led governance and monitoring [#SRC:e46640365e209635] [#TGT:abeb4286e603ff85].",[First sentence moved to 2.4B ] The PRA’s expectations for internal credit assessments are expanded on in paragraphs 2.8A to 2.8N below.,"Where some or all of the internal credit assessment process is outsourced, the PRA expects firms also to demonstrate the effectiveness of the systems and processes that the outsourcer has in place, including validation, in order to ensure that outsourced internal credit assessments for assets satisfy the expectations set out in paragraphs 2.8A to 2.8M above and that the requirements of Rules 7.1A , 7.2A and 7.5 to 7.8 in the Conditions Governing Business Part of the PRA Rulebook are also satisfied. Firms should provide evidence that appropriate oversight systems and processes including governance are in place and have been carried out effectively for outsourced credit assessments.",SCHEMA,,basic,UKFIN,hard_enriched,e46640365e209635,abeb4286e603ff85,,,e46640365e209635,abeb4286e603ff85,,,,,HV0194,03497c23b194dce8,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-UKFIN-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

030f9d61abd3125f,"When designing its policy for managing positions and collateral across relevant entities, what must a firm set out about the factors that determine when positions are offset or closed and the expected timeline for doing so, and how must it ensure it can identify legal and operational features that affect collateral management, including transfers within the group and to third parties?","A firm should document, in its policy, the specific factors it will use to decide when a position should be offset or closed, and it should also specify the expected timeline for taking those actions, so that position management is governed by clear decision criteria and time expectations [#SRC:0fc504dca2fa1201]. This policy should sit within effective, consolidated risk management oversight across the relevant entities and be calibrated to a level commensurate with the structure of the relevant business division, so that the consolidation point matches how seniority and reporting lines are organised [#SRC:0fc504dca2fa1201]. In parallel, the firm should be able to identify legal and operational features that impact the management of collateral, including features affecting the transfer of collateral both within the group and to third parties, so that collateral movements and constraints are understood and can be managed in practice [#TGT:08d9645cfabc4417]. Taken together, the policy’s decision factors and timelines for offsetting/closing positions should be operationally workable in light of those identified legal and operational constraints on collateral transfers [#SRC:0fc504dca2fa1201] [#TGT:08d9645cfabc4417].","d) effective, consolidated risk management oversight is in place across the relevant entities. This consolidated risk management should be set at a level that is commensurate with the structure of the relevant business division. As an example, if there are two senior business heads and they both report directly to the global business head, that would be the appropriate level. But if they are two more junior business heads, the consolidation should occur at a lower level. In addition, firms should consider what they need to manage their risks holistically both in business-as-usual and in a crisis. It is generally considered good practice to have a free flow of collateral between desks, and this is particularly helpful in a crisis so banks may be able to avoid hedging with the market externally unnecessarily. Similarly, there may be advantages to having the ability to reduce offsetting inventory positions by way of periodic inter-affiliate transactions, and the ability to pool collateral between entities and branches for centralised financing and short-covering purposes. The firm’s policy should set out the factors determining when a position should be offset or closed and the expected timeline for taking such actions. This approach is consistent with the Bank of England’s expectations under the UK Resolution Assessment Framework. 39","39. Firms should also be able to identify any legal and operational features that impact the management of collateral, including the transfer of collateral both within the group and to third parties”. See Resolvability Assessment of Major UK Banks 2024. https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/financial-stability/resolution/resolvability-assessment-framework/resovability-assessment-of-major-uk-banks-2024",SCHEMA,,professional,UKFIN,hard_enriched,0fc504dca2fa1201,08d9645cfabc4417,,,0fc504dca2fa1201,08d9645cfabc4417,,,,,HV0195,030f9d61abd3125f,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-UKFIN-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

dfdee79151ab30be,"If an outsourcing deal is material and the PRA expects the written contract to cover areas like data security, audit and access rights, sub-outsourcing, and business continuity and exit, what do banks and insurers have to do about putting the outsourcing arrangement in writing?","Banks and insurers have to make sure the outsourcing arrangement is set out in a written agreement, and for material outsourcing that written agreement should cover the minimum areas the PRA expects. In practice, this means the firm should not only have a signed written contract for the outsourcing arrangement, but also ensure the contract includes terms dealing with data security, access, audit and information rights, sub-outsourcing, and business continuity and exit strategies, because these are identified as the minimum areas the PRA expects written agreements relating to material outsourcing to address [#SRC:7ee6ded449cc3c29]. Separately, there is a baseline requirement that all outsourcing arrangements must be set out in a written agreement for banks and insurers [#TGT:9752e97c411082aa]. Read together, the firm should treat the written agreement as the main control document: it must exist for every outsourcing arrangement, and for material outsourcing it should be detailed enough to cover the specific minimum topics the PRA expects.","Chapter 6 lists the areas that the PRA expects written agreements relating to material outsourcing to address as a minimum. The following four areas are then examined in detail in Chapters 7–10: data security ( Chapter 7 ); access, audit, and information rights ( Chapter 8 ); sub-outsourcing ( Chapter 9 ); and business continuity and exit strategies ( Chapter 10 ).","In line with Article 31(3) of MODR (banks) and Conditions Governing Business 7.5(3) (insurers), all outsourcing arrangements must be set out in a written agreement.",SCHEMA,,basic,UKFIN,hard_enriched,7ee6ded449cc3c29,9752e97c411082aa,,,7ee6ded449cc3c29,9752e97c411082aa,,,,,HV0196,dfdee79151ab30be,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-UKFIN-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

2a4713a2b280c0a3,"When the PRA sets and collects periodic fees each year to recover its Annual Funding Requirement, how should the Annual Funding Requirement be defined in terms of the types of regulatory costs it reflects, and what category of budgeted costs must be excluded from that definition?","For the purpose of periodic fees that are set by the PRA and collected each year to recover the PRA’s Annual Funding Requirement, the Annual Funding Requirement should be defined by reference to the cost categories it is intended to recover and the cost categories it expressly does not recover. On the inclusion side, the Annual Funding Requirement reflects the costs relating to Ongoing Regulatory Activities, meaning the costs the PRA incurs in performing its functions as regulator, and it may also reflect exceptional costs (for example, costs arising from recent changes in the scope of regulation) where those exceptional costs are not incorporated into Ongoing Regulatory Activities costs [#SRC:85621563f8cf9168]. On the exclusion side, the Annual Funding Requirement does not include any special project fee costs where those costs are budgeted, so those budgeted special project fee costs must be kept outside the Annual Funding Requirement even though periodic fees are collected to recover it [#TGT:230a19b54b13bd74]. Taken together, this means the Annual Funding Requirement is a funding measure tied to ongoing regulatory and certain exceptional regulatory costs, but it is not a vehicle for recovering budgeted special project fee costs.","Periodic fees are set by the PRA and collected each year in order to recover the PRA’s Annual Funding Requirement (AFR). The AFR reflects: 1 • costs relating to Ongoing Regulatory Activities (ORA), being the costs which the PRA incurs in performing its functions as regulator; and • any exceptional costs (eg to reflect recent changes in the scope of regulation) not incorporated into ORA costs.","1. Note: the AFR does not include any special project fee (SPF) costs, where these are budgeted.",SCHEMA,,professional,UKFIN,hard_enriched,85621563f8cf9168,230a19b54b13bd74,,,85621563f8cf9168,230a19b54b13bd74,,,,,HV0197,2a4713a2b280c0a3,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-UKFIN-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

e48221c2f2cc8ff4,"For undertakings referred to in the specified category, and excluding undertakings covered by the separate carve-out, what must the equity risk sub-module include when determining the relevant amount under the referenced valuation and standard formula provisions?","For undertakings referred to in the specified category, the scope condition is that the approach applies to those undertakings except where they fall within the separate exclusion for undertakings covered by the carve-out, and the amount is to be determined in accordance with the referenced valuation and standard formula provisions [#SRC:a19de5e5078439a5]. Within that scoped determination, the equity risk sub-module must be structured to include distinct risk sub-modules covering type 1 equities and type 2 equities, and it must also include dedicated risk sub-modules for qualifying infrastructure equities and for qualifying infrastructure corporate equities [#TGT:8a3ef0d20b9b4dac]. In practice, this means that, for an undertaking that is in-scope (i.e., within the referred category and not within the carve-out), the equity risk component cannot be treated as a single undifferentiated charge; it must be decomposed into the four specified equity categories so that the amount determined under the referenced framework reflects each required sub-module. The exclusion matters because undertakings within the carve-out are not subject to this scoped determination pathway [#SRC:a19de5e5078439a5].","(4) for undertakings referred to in 11.1A(6) , other than undertakings covered by point (5) of this rule, the amount determined in accordance with Valuation 9 and Solvency Capital Requirement – Standard Formula 3D7 - 3D11 , 3D26 – 3D31 and 3D32 ; and","The equity risk sub-module must include a risk sub-module for type 1 equities, a risk sub-module for type 2 equities, a risk sub-module for qualifying infrastructure equities and a risk sub-module for qualifying infrastructure corporate equities.",SCHEMA,,professional,UKFIN,hard_enriched,a19de5e5078439a5,8a3ef0d20b9b4dac,,,a19de5e5078439a5,8a3ef0d20b9b4dac,,,,,HV0198,e48221c2f2cc8ff4,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-UKFIN-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

26739e970ab793af,"If an undertaking wants to set up or change a debt securities programme to issue something the firm plans to count as basic own funds for the group SCR, what does the firm have to check about earlier information it gave to the PRA and about changes in law, and what must the programme say about what each instrument issued under it is?","If an undertaking proposes to establish or amend a debt securities programme to issue an item the firm intends to include within the basic own funds forming the own funds eligible for the group SCR, the firm must ensure the programme meets conditions that protect both regulatory compliance and the intended own-funds treatment [#TGT:d43cd8def623245e]. First, the firm must make sure the programme still complies even if there have been changes in law or regulation, or in how those rules are interpreted or applied, since the last time the programme was notified; and the firm must also ensure that the information previously notified to the PRA about the programme is not affected by those changes [#SRC:a0002fe3a6bea784]. Second, the firm must ensure the programme’s terms require that any instrument issued under the programme constitutes basic own funds, so that instruments issued pursuant to the programme match the firm’s intention to include them within basic own funds for group SCR eligibility [#SRC:a0002fe3a6bea784]. Together, these points describe what the firm must ensure when it is proposing to set up or change the programme for that purpose [#TGT:d43cd8def623245e].","(b) the programme complies with, and the information previously notified to the PRA in accordance with 6.4 in relation to the programme is unaffected by, any changes in law or regulation, or the interpretation or application of either, coming into effect since the last notification in accordance with 6.4 ; and (c) any instrument issued pursuant to the programme must, under the terms of the programme, constitute basic own funds ; and","If an undertaking proposes to establish or amend a debt securities programme for the issue of an item which the firm intends to include within the basic own funds forming the own funds eligible for the group SCR , the firm must:",SCHEMA,,basic,UKFIN,hard_enriched,a0002fe3a6bea784,d43cd8def623245e,,,a0002fe3a6bea784,d43cd8def623245e,,,,,HV0199,26739e970ab793af,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-UKFIN-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,

291b3770ae2bb00b,"When providing resolution planning information about the group’s preparations, what must the firm do to ensure it is prepared for an orderly resolution with minimal disruption of critical services, and how should it respond if the PRA and the Bank as resolution authority—after discussing with one or both among the home state supervisor and home resolution authority—determine that additional information is required?","The firm must ensure that its resolution planning materials describe and support concrete preparations that enable the firm to be resolved in an orderly manner, if needed, while minimising disruption to critical services [#TGT:ba7a108ec58f63f0]. In practice, this means the firm’s resolution planning information should cover the group’s preparations for resolution and present them in a way that demonstrates readiness for orderly resolution outcomes, rather than treating the submission as a purely descriptive exercise [#SRC:b277461e673dbd9a]. The firm should also be prepared for supervisory follow-up: the PRA and the Bank as resolution authority may engage with external authorities by discussing the firm’s position with one or both among the home state supervisor and home resolution authority, and then assess whether the firm needs to provide further information [#SRC:b277461e673dbd9a]. Accordingly, the firm should maintain its resolution planning information so it can promptly supply any additional information requested, ensuring that any supplemental materials continue to evidence the firm’s preparedness for resolution and its ability to protect continuity of critical services [#TGT:ba7a108ec58f63f0].","resolution planning, including information regarding the group’s preparations for resolution consistent with Fundamental Rule 8 (the PRA, and the Bank as resolution authority, will discuss with one or both among the home state supervisor and home resolution authority, and then consider if any additional information is required from the firm).","Fundamental Rule 8: A firm must prepare for resolution so, if the need arises, it can be resolved in an orderly manner with a minimum disruption of critical services.",SCHEMA,,professional,UKFIN,hard_enriched,b277461e673dbd9a,ba7a108ec58f63f0,,,b277461e673dbd9a,ba7a108ec58f63f0,,,,,HV0200,291b3770ae2bb00b,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-UKFIN-ALL/final.jsonl,,,,
